name: UNCF Scholarships
description: Various deadlines for various UNCF-sponsored scholarships. Browse the UNCF scholarship portal to find the programs you are eligible for.

name: GE-Reagan Foundation Scholarship
description: The GE-Reagan Foundation Scholarship is a $10,000 renewable scholarship opportunity (up to $40,000) open to seniors who showcase leadership, drive, integrity, and citizenship. Recipients also join the Reagan Academy network of exceptional students and young professionals who desire to lead, serve, and have a positive impact on their communities.

name: AIAA Roger W. Kahn Scholarship
description: In honor of Roger Kahn for his work in aviation and entertainment, the Institute of the Aeronautical Sciences will be awarding four $10,000 scholarships to high school seniors who will enroll in an engineering major to pursue a career in aerospace. The scholarship includes a trip to the AIAA Awards Gala and a mentor in AIAA to help guide the student to achieve a career in aerospace. In order to be eligible, members should have a minimum high school GPA of 3.5 and have demonstrated interest in aerospace through extracurricular activities. To apply, you need to submit a transcript, a one-page statement that describes STEM-related studies or extracurricular activities, an application form, and a letter of recommendation from a STEM educator/mentor.

name: William G. Ericson Photography Competition & Scholarship
description: PCC features more than 31 finalists to sponsor photographic art competitions. High school seniors have the opportunity to win up to $7,000. In order to qualify you must submit photo submissions (analog or digital camera) that must fit within a 16 x 16 area and write a 100-word maximum statement on how the funds will help your photography education. $40,000 was awarded in 2025.

name: Jackie Robinson Scholarship
description: JRF Scholars receive college scholarships of up to $35,000 over four years and are sponsored to attend JRF's annual, four-day "Mentoring and Leadership Conference" in New York City. Scholars also benefit from a comprehensive program that includes career guidance, internship and job placement, travel abroad, and leadership and practical life skills training.

name: Sons of Norway Foundation Scholarships
description: The Sons of Norway Foundation awards 35+ scholarships to students each year and promotes cultural exchange and supports education to help students prepare the next generation of workers. These scholarships award $1,000 to full tuition awards. The eligibility for applicants for all scholarships is very diverse.

name: Asian & Pacific Islander American (APIA) Scholars Scholarship
description: Asian & Pacific Islander American (APIA) Scholars offer a range of scholarships to support students who identify as Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander (AANHPI). Awards vary from $2,500 to $20,000.

name: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship
description: A 2-for-1 opportunity for seniors. Get a $40,000 scholarship ($10,000/year) towards an undergraduate degree in computer science and a guaranteed summer internship at Amazon. This one is for future engineers planning to earn a bachelor's degree in a computer science related field of study from an accredited 4-year college or from a 2-year college intending to transfer to a 4-year college. Also required: a 3.0 cumulative GPA and eligibility to work in the US.

name: The Edison Scholars Program
description: The Edison Scholars Program recognizes students who want to be makers of tomorrow — the dreamers, inventors, guardians and pioneers — those who dare to be great. Each year, Edison International awards $50,000 college scholarships to 30 high school seniors to help them follow their dreams in science, technology, engineering or math (STEM) and empower them to change the world. Applicants must be a high school senior with at least a cumulative 3.0 GPA, plan to pursue studies in the STEM fields at a four-year accredited college or university, and show financial need. Eligible STEM majors include computer and information systems, engineering, engineering technology, management information systems, mathematics, natural resources and conservation, and physical sciences. Applicants must live in Southern California Edison's service territory. The top 50 finalists will be required to submit a short video and potentially participate in a final interview. Dependents of Edison International and SCE employees and retirees are not eligible.

name: Melvin Kruger Endowed Scholarship (Roofing Alliance)
description: $1,000-$5,000 scholarships! The Roofing Alliance Melvin Kruger Endowed Scholarship Program offers three scholarship opportunities. All categories are open to employees of roofing industry companies, their spouses and their dependent children, as well as construction management students enrolled at the undergraduate level or students enrolled in CTE programs or schools (regardless of industry affiliation).

name: Union Plus Scholarship
description: $4,000 - 199 awards. Since 1991, the Union Plus Scholarship Program has awarded more than $5.2 million to students of working families who want to begin or continue their post-secondary education. More than 3,600 families have benefited from this commitment to higher education. The Union Plus Scholarship Program is offered through the Union Plus Education Foundation, supported in part by contributions from the provider of the Union Plus Credit Card. (You do not need to be a Union Plus Credit Card holder to apply for this scholarship.)

name: Daughters of the American Revolution (DAR) Scholarships
description: $1,500-$25,000 scholarships. One application for various scholarships! Sign up and create an account on the DAR scholarship portal to see the applications.

name: California Association of Collectors Educational Scholarship Foundation (CACESF) Scholarship
description: CACESF's scholarship contest is open to current high school JUNIORS and seniors who will be attending any accredited public or private college, university, or trade school within 12 months of graduation. $2,500 First Award, $2,000 Second Award, and $1,500 Third Awards given. All applicants must write an original essay on the following topic: The importance of establishing and maintaining good financial credit during your college years. Essay guidelines: entries must be typed, 12-point font, double spaced, and be between 700 and 1,000 words. All essays must include the word count at the top of the document. Please DO NOT put your personal information on any page.

name: California State PTA Graduating High School Senior Scholarships
description: The California State PTA Graduating High School Senior Scholarship offers two types of scholarships: the Volunteer Service Scholarship and the Dr. Ralph E. White Graduating Senior Scholarship for students who intend to pursue careers in the medical field. Applications are due February 1 at midnight.

name: Armenian American Scholarship Guide (ANCA)
description: The ANCA is committed to helping Armenian students advance their education by sharing information about scholarships available at various academic institutions and at different levels of learning. Students are encouraged to apply to all scholarships for which they are eligible. Some scholarships have specific school and field of study requirements. See the guide for the numerous opportunities with various deadline dates.

name: CSEA Chapter 122 Scholarship
description: Scholarship applications are accepted each year for CSEA Chapter 122. The scholarships are available to all current CSEA members in Chapter 122 and their immediate family. The scholarship award may vary each year, but the award in 2023 from Chapter 122 was $600. This amount may be divided among one or more recipients.

name: The Media Plan Case Competition (Media Scholars)
description: The Media Plan Case Competition challenges students to think strategically and dive into the deep end of marketing impressions, numbers and budgets. Finalists receive an all-expenses-paid, week-long professional development experience in Washington D.C. and compete for the National Excellence in Media Award and $18,500 in scholarships.

name: Distinguished Young Women of Los Angeles County
description: Distinguished Young Women of Los Angeles County offers college-granted scholarships. See the list of college-granted scholarships to find which colleges might be your opportunity to apply and win.

name: Morton Gould Young Composer Awards (ASCAP Foundation)
description: The ASCAP Foundation Morton Gould Young Composer Awards (the "Awards") honor the late Pulitzer Prize-winning composer and The ASCAP Foundation's former president Morton Gould's lifelong commitment to encouraging young creators. Open to composers of original, classical concert music, the Awards encourage developing music creators during the earliest stages of their careers.

name: Certified Wellness Coach Scholarships (HCAI)
description: Annual scholarships administered by California's Department of Health Care Access and Information, covering one year of education at a California university or community college with a maximum award of $35,000 per student. Recipients must be willing to study human services, addiction studies or social work and after graduation commit to a service obligation for one year as a Certified Wellness Coach.

name: La Cañada Thursday Club Foundation Scholarships
description: TWO different scholarship opportunities - pick one or the other. One of the main philanthropic projects of the La Cañada Thursday Club Foundation is to further the youth of our community in their academic endeavors. Each year, they offer: 1) the La Cañada Thursday Club Foundation Scholarship (academic excellence, community service, potential for success) and 2) the La Cañada Thursday Club Foundation Greenawalt Scholarship (triumphed over an obstacle, hardship or extenuating circumstance; potential for success). Applicants must be a graduating high school senior and reside or attend a high school within the city of La Cañada Flintridge for both scholarships. Letters of recommendation and transcripts are due shortly after the application deadline.

name: Hispanic Scholarship Fund (HSF) Scholar Program
description: HSF selects 10,000 outstanding students as HSF Scholars from a broad and talented pool of applicants every year. HSF Scholars are a part of an unrivaled group of 25,000+ Scholars from 50 states, and more than 1,200 institutions, who make up the current HSF Scholar network. Requirements: must be of Hispanic heritage; U.S. citizen, permanent legal resident, or DACA; minimum of 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale (or equivalent) for high school students (2.5 for college and graduate students); plan to enroll full-time in an accredited, public or not-for-profit, four-year university, or graduate school, in the U.S.; submit the FAFSA or state-based financial aid forms.

name: McDonald's HACER National Scholarship
description: To date, more than $33 million in McDonald's HACER® National Scholarships have been awarded to Hispanic students across the country. The McDonald's HACER® National Scholarship Program offers scholarships to up to 30 outstanding Hispanic students from all over the country, and continues to provide educational opportunities to help narrow the gap that exists for Hispanic college-bound students, further reinforcing McDonald's long-standing commitment to feeding and fostering the diverse communities it serves. There are three tiers of funds, aimed to help recipients finance their college tuition. Tier 1 recipients are awarded up to $100,000. Tier 2 recipients receive $20,000 or $10,000 and Tier 3 recipients receive $5,000. Recipients are selected based on their academic achievement, community involvement, personal statement and financial need.

name: Yardi Scholars for Environmental Justice (UCSB)
description: For seniors who applied to UCSB and are interested in creating sustainable environmental solutions, this four-year scholarship is here to help you create a debt-free path to a UCSB degree. An information session is typically held in late January.

name: KFC REACH Educational Grant Program
description: $3,000 - 50 awards. The KFC REACH Educational Grant Program helps KFC restaurant employees pursue their dreams of going to college. Apply for up to $20,000 in scholarships to attend the two- or four-year college, trade school or graduate school of your choice. You can re-apply and potentially win a scholarship year after year. This is a competitive program, meaning not everyone who applies will receive a scholarship.

name: Gordon A. Rich Memorial Scholarship
description: $60,000 (the amount of each GAR award is determined by financial need). Gordon A. Rich was a committed supporter of people of lesser means and limited opportunities. While he was alive, he donated enormous amounts of his incredible energy, passion and resources to help improve their conditions. The Gordon A. Rich Memorial Foundation (GAR) intends to carry on that commitment. Requirements: 1. Applicants must be dependent children of full-time employees in the financial services industry (commercial banks, investment banks, securities brokerage firms, insurance companies, fund and asset management companies, credit card and finance companies and similar businesses as determined by the Foundation). Employees must be presently employed with at least five years of experience working in the financial sector. 2. Students must be graduating high school seniors who are enrolling as full-time first-year students in pursuit of a four-year bachelor's degree at an accredited college/university in the United States. 3. Students must have a minimum grade point average of 3.5 (on a 4.0 scale) and rank in the top 20% of their class. 4. Students must demonstrate financial need. 5. Students must be a US citizen or legal resident.

name: Military Benefit Association (MBA) Scholarship
description: This scholarship is giving senior applicants associated with the Military Benefit Association a chance to win a $3,000 scholarship. Up to 30 people can win this scholarship. Applicants must have a minimum 2.5 GPA.

name: Coast Guard Exchange (CGX) Scholarship Program
description: The Coast Guard Exchange Scholarship Program provides scholarships to students who are dependents of Coast Guard active duty, reserve, and military retired members, current civilian NAF and APF employees, and current Coast Guard Auxiliarists. The applicant must be a senior.

name: Fred M. Young Sr. SAE Engineering Scholarship
description: Fred M. Young Sr., the one who started The Young Radiator Co., wanted to provide students in the future engineering workforce support to pursue their engineering/related science degree. Seniors must have an unweighted 3.75 GPA, two letters of recommendation, have served in a leadership role, and be able to detail how 2 traits of an engineer apply to them.

name: Tau Beta Pi SAE Engineering Scholarship
description: Tau Beta Pi Association, the world's largest engineering society, wants to welcome seniors with a minimum unweighted 3.75 GPA who want to pursue an engineering or related science degree through an ABET-accredited program with a chance to win $1,500. Up to 6 applicants can win this scholarship. Letters of recommendation and community service project(s) must be submitted as well. Applications open February 1 and are due February 28.

name: LA Military Charitable Fund (LAMCF) Scholarship
description: This program is for graduating high school seniors who are dependents of an active duty/retired/100% disabled Armed Forces member or Department of Defense civilian. The program awarded up to $45,500 in scholarships. The application and eligibility requirements are embedded in the linked document.

name: La Cañada Council PTA & First District PTA Commemorative Senior Scholarship
description: The La Cañada Council PTA Scholarship application is included with the First District PTA Commemorative Scholarship application; all applications will be considered for LC Council AND First District PTA. First District PTA (FDPTA) awards scholarships of $800 to support students who are planning to attend a community college, trade or tech school, or a four-year college or university in the fall. Applicants must be current graduating high school seniors or college students, members of their high school or college PTA/PTSA, have a GPA of at least 2.0, and should have a strong record of community service and/or school activities, hold an after school, part-time, or summer job, and/or manage extra home responsibilities. The application must be submitted via the online form; no physical copies will be accepted. The application includes a personal statement (limited to 500 words) and four required uploads: a legible copy of the student's current PTA/PTSA membership card, a reference form, a letter of recommendation, and the student's high school or college transcript. PTSA student memberships can be purchased on the LCHS PTSA website, and membership cards can be picked up in the College & Career Center from Mrs. Proctor.

name: American Legion Eagle Scout of the Year Scholarship
description: $10,000 award to the winner; three runners-up will be granted $2,500 each. The American Legion Eagle Scout of the Year nomination window is from November 1st to March 1st, annually. Nomination packets must be received by each applicant's respective American Legion Department (state) no later than March 1st. Each Department Selection Committee will determine the Eagle Scout judged to be the best in their state and send that packet to The American Legion National Headquarters no later than April 1st. To be eligible for the scholarship a student must: A) have reached their 15th birthday and be enrolled in high school; B) be a registered active member of a Boy Scouts of America unit that is chartered to an American Legion post, American Legion Auxiliary unit or Sons of The American Legion squadron.

name: AFSA National High School Essay Contest
description: The American Foreign Service Association's National High School Essay Contest is open to all high school students whose parents are not in the Foreign Service. The winner receives $2,500, a trip to Washington, D.C. to meet a member of the State Department's leadership and a full scholarship for a Semester at Sea educational voyage. The runner-up receives $1,250 and a full scholarship to attend the summer session of National Student Leadership Conference's International Diplomacy Program.

name: Sons and Daughters of Italy in America (OSIA California) Scholarships
description: Offering academic and athletic scholarships for graduating seniors. Awards are open to students who are wholly or partially of Italian descent and will be enrolling in an accredited trade school, college, university or community college in the fall. There is an Academic Scholarship application, an Athletic Scholarship for students pursuing a degree in sports or a sports-related field, a Career Education Scholarship, and an Italian Language Study Grant Application.

name: Life Lessons Scholarship Program (Life Happens)
description: $15,000 (29 awards). A college education is already a major financial challenge for most American families, but it becomes infinitely more difficult for a student when a parent dies, leaving little or no life insurance. Recognizing the character and perseverance that so many young people show in the face of such adversity, Life Happens sponsors the annual Life Lessons Scholarship Program for college students and college-bound high school seniors. Qualified entrants who submit essays or videos about how the death of a parent impacted their lives are eligible for scholarship money. Over two and a half million dollars in college scholarships have been awarded over the years. Eligibility requirements: between 17-24 years of age; have experienced the death of a parent or legal guardian; will be attending college, university or trade school in the US or Puerto Rico in the upcoming fall semester; pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree; legal resident of the United States or Puerto Rico; no employees or household members employed by The Life and Health Insurance Foundation or its affiliates; have parent's or legal guardian's permission to enter if under age 18.

name: Horatio Alger Association Scholarships
description: As one of the nation's largest need-based college scholarship programs in the country, the Horatio Alger Scholarships specifically assist high school students who have faced and overcome great obstacles in their young lives. Seniors: the association offers several scholarships that either require an applicant to pursue a specific degree or attend a specific university. These specialized programs are funded through the generosity of individual Horatio Alger Members. Juniors: there are a number of scholarships specifically for juniors, including state scholarships valued at $10,000, $25,000 national scholarships, and $2,500 for those who have a strong commitment to pursue and complete a career or technical program.

name: Gallery Collection Create-A-Greeting-Card Scholarship
description: $10,000. Would you like your artwork featured by the leading publisher of premium quality cards in the United States? Here's your chance! Enter the annual Create-A-Greeting-Card $10,000 contest. Design a greeting card for the opportunity to win yourself a $10,000 scholarship and $1,000 for your school. Plus, your winning entry will be made into a bona fide greeting card by The Gallery Collection.

name: Dr. John & Mae Benjamin Scholarship (Community Foundation of the Verdugos)
description: The Dr. John & Mae Benjamin Scholarship benefits a student pursuing a medical career. Offered through the Community Foundation of the Verdugos.

name: "Big Man" Fritsche Scholarship (Community Foundation of the Verdugos)
description: This award is for a student pursuing a vocational study (career technical path with examples that include woodworking, auto mechanics, plumbing, landscaping, dental hygienist, vet tech, electrical, cosmetology, culinary arts, etc.) toward achieving whatever dream may be in their future. A recipient of this scholarship must reside in and graduate from a public/private high school in the Verdugo Region (Burbank, Glendale, foothill communities of Sunland, Tujunga, La Crescenta, La Cañada Flintridge, Montrose, and Verdugo City). The student must be pursuing a certificate or degree from a non-profit, accredited institution in a career technical field (two or three-year program). This award is not for a student enrolling in a four-year college or university. Financial need will be considered. The student should show an entrepreneurial aptitude, a potential for achievement and evidence of self-motivation. Qualified students may be selected for an in-person interview. Average number of awards: 2. Average amount of awards: up to $2,000. Applicants provide a brief personal statement about what they find motivating, interesting and/or fulfilling about the career path they plan to pursue.

name: Asian Pacific Fund Scholarships
description: There are several scholarship possibilities, each tailored to reflect the donor's personal interests, whether targeted to specific ethnicities, career paths, or backgrounds. Amounts range from $1,000 to $20,000. Scholarships include the Banatao Family Filipino American Education Fund, the Shui Kuen and Allen Chin Scholarship, the Hsiao Memorial Social Sciences Scholarship, and the Helen and L.S. Wong Memorial Scholarship.

name: Japanese American Citizens League (JACL) National Scholarship Program
description: The Japanese American Citizens League currently offers over 30 scholarships with an annual total of over $70,000. Applicants must be an active JACL member at either an individual or student youth level. Separate applications are available for college freshmen, general applicants, and creative & performing arts. Note: the application will not save or reload, so please fill it out in one sitting.

name: John & Elsie Krikorian / Women Achievers Journalism Scholarship (Community Foundation of the Verdugos)
description: John and Elsie Krikorian were the founders and editors of Business Life Magazine that provided Burbank, Glendale, Pasadena, and Foothill communities with local business news for over 25 years. With their passing, it inspired the creation of a scholarship for a female student pursuing a career in journalism, marketing, or business management. Up to 2 people can get $500. You need to fill out your FAFSA, submit a recommendation letter, type an essay about your goals in their respective area, and input a transcript and a resume.

name: Christopher A. Burrows Memorial Scholarship (Community Foundation of the Verdugos)
description: The creation of this scholarship was made to honor Chris Burrows, a La Cañada resident who had a brain tumor and was a friend, husband, and father to many. This scholarship is awarded to students who live in La Cañada Flintridge or La Crescenta who have high academic and extracurricular achievements, "a zest for life", and strong character. 3-5 people can win up to $2,500 if they submit a personal statement about their character and goals. The Christopher A. Burrows Scholarship committee considers your personal statement/essays to be the most important part of your application. Personal Statement #1: a paragraph that addresses your interest in this particular scholarship, why you believe you would be a worthy recipient, and how this scholarship will make a difference to you financially. Personal Statement #2: either your favorite college application essay that tells about yourself, or a personal statement that discusses your background, your goals, why these goals are important to you, and how and why you believe you will achieve them.

name: The First Christian Church of Glendale Scholarship (Community Foundation of the Verdugos)
description: Graduating seniors with a minimum 2.5 GPA and a minimum of 13 years residency around the La Cañada Flintridge area that believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and their personal Savior can win up to $1,500 as long as they provide a personal essay explaining their religious belief that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and their personal Savior and their view on what it means to be an American.

name: Community Foundation of the Verdugos Scholarships
description: Created by individuals and organizations to assist students who are pursuing a higher education. Each scholarship has specific eligibility criteria, including students who are pursuing a medical career, students who live or go to school in La Cañada, or students who are fluent in Spanish and English... and more! See the foundation's site for the various scholarships' requirements and to apply.

name: Gonzales-Harris Bilingual Scholarship (Community Foundation of the Verdugos)
description: The Gonzalez sisters have a reputation for giving back to others. In turn, they decided to give back to the youth and create a scholarship for students that have a minimum 3.5 GPA, have proof of US citizenship, and are able to demonstrate fluency in both Spanish and English. An interview will be scheduled to assess the student's Spanish fluency if qualified. A personal statement highlighting the importance of education and how you will contribute back to the community will need to be submitted as well for this scholarship awarding $6,000.

name: Shirley & Joel Youngquist Nursing Scholarship (Community Foundation of the Verdugos / GCC)
description: Memorializes Shirley's long career in the field of nursing. It is intended for a student in the GCC nursing program who has had residency in Glendale, La Cañada Flintridge, La Crescenta, Montrose or Verdugo City for the past three years. Available through Glendale Community College; visit the GCC Scholarship Office or contact them at 818-240-1000 x5591.

name: Chuck Benedict Memorial Journalism Scholarship (Community Foundation of the Verdugos / GCC)
description: Recognizes the late Chuck Benedict who was a well-known sports broadcaster in the Los Angeles area. His wife Fran and sons Rick and Steve established this fund to recognize an aspiring journalism student who is pursuing a specific interest in sports journalism. Available through Glendale Community College; visit the GCC Scholarship Office or contact them at 818-240-1000 x5591.

name: California Credit Union Annual Scholarship Program
description: The credit union will award 10 students within LA and Orange County with a scholarship of $1,000 each. High school seniors and community college students transferring to a four-year university who maintain a minimum grade point average of 3.0 are eligible to participate. Selection criteria include academic performance, school or community involvement, a letter of recommendation, and an essay submission (1 of 3 topics).

name: AFSA Scholarships (American Foreign Service Association)
description: The AFSA Scholarship Program offers college aid to children of AFSA members whose parents are/were Foreign Service employees. Nearly $370,000 in Merit and Financial Aid scholarships will be awarded in total. Merit and Financial Aid scholarships have separate deadlines (Merit in early March, Financial Aid in mid-April).

name: Foothills Community Scholarship Foundation of La Cañada Flintridge (FCSF)
description: FCSF is an all-volunteer organization that has scholarships ranging from $1,000 to $3,000 for local students and a mission to inspire students to achieve their full potential. Believing there is an abundance of scholarships awarded to the top GPA students, FCSF seeks to identify, support and encourage higher education for students who have a high level of integrity, are committed, are self-motivated, and who persevere even in adversity.

name: La Cañada Teachers Association (LCTA) Scholarships
description: The La Cañada Teachers Association offers scholarships to seniors in eight different categories. All information as well as the application itself can be found in the LCTA Scholarship Google Classroom (join code: vzwuxxbx). If your application is selected to move forward, in-person interviews will be conducted on campus the following week.

name: President Gerald R. Ford Student Writing Challenge
description: All high school students are invited to write a 500-750 word essay for a scholarship of up to $2,500. This essay is focused on following Ford's footsteps to answer the call to service. Students are encouraged to research President Ford.

name: PG&E Better Together STEM Scholarship
description: Committed to supporting inclusive programs rooted in the values of People, Planet and Prosperity, PG&E and The PG&E Corporation Foundation offer a wide range of scholarships to help the next generation of Californians succeed and innovate in Science, Technology, Engineering and Math (STEM) based majors and other disciplines. The PG&E Corporation Foundation offers Better Together STEM Scholarships of $2,500 or $10,000 to students pursuing STEM-related studies at universities in California. Students must be California residents and PG&E customers at the time of application. Students enrolled in Engineering (electrical, mechanical, industrial, environmental, power and/or energy), Computer Science/Information Systems/Cyber Security, and Environmental Science majors are eligible.

name: IAPD Scholarship Program
description: $5,000 - 17 awards. The IAPD Charitable Foundation was established in 1981 as a non-profit tax exempt corporation to provide scholarships at the undergraduate and graduate degree levels to employees of IAPD member firms and their children, as well as students enrolled in a professional sales program (major, minor or concentration). Each year, worthy recipients are awarded up to US$5,000 to provide meaningful financial support for their college/university education.

name: Dr. Arthur A. Kezian DDS Science Scholarship
description: $1,200 - 1 award. The Dr. Arthur A. Kezian DDS Science Scholarship will be awarding $1,200 to help deserving science students. Applicants are required to be high school seniors to graduate students in university, majoring in a science field and pursuing advanced education. Applications will be reviewed by the scholarship committee and will be awarded based on academic merit, community service, and financial need. To be eligible you must be at least 18 years of age (based on the date of the deadline).

name: The Bill and Linda James Scholarship (Altadena Arts)
description: Honors the lives and legacies of two proud Pasadena/Altadena residents whose deep roots in the community shaped generations that followed. To be eligible for this award, scholars must: be a resident of one of the Eaton Fire impact zones (Altadena, Pasadena, or Sierra Madre) at the time of the fire; be impacted by the Eaton Fire through loss or damage of home, loss of family or personal income, and/or temporary or permanent displacement; be in good academic standing with a minimum 2.5 GPA or higher; be a high school senior or current college student attending a 2-year or 4-year accredited institution of higher education; and demonstrate leadership, volunteer, civic, or other involvement in the community.

name: Automotive Aftermarket Scholarships Central
description: If you're a full-time student at a U.S. college or university or an ASE/NATEF Certified post-secondary automotive, heavy duty, or collision repair school you can apply. Your complete scholarship application will be automatically considered by the University of the Aftermarket Foundation and several other organizations for several scholarship opportunities.

name: Italian Catholic Federation (ICF) First Year Scholarship
description: Sponsored by the Italian Catholic Federation, this scholarship rewards students who are Roman Catholic and are either of Italian descent or who have parents, guardians, or grandparents as members of the Italian Catholic Federation. Students must achieve a total cumulative GPA of at least 3.2. First year scholarships in the amount of $500 will be awarded to approximately 130 applicants. First year scholarship winners are eligible for second, third, and fourth year awards of $600, $700, and $1,000 respectively.

name: National CCAA First-Year Scholarship
description: A one-time, $1,000 award that is given to 16 randomly selected high school seniors from various geographic regions who will attend one of the National CCAA member institutions in the fall.

name: The Men's College Scholarship (Foundation for Fraternal Excellence)
description: The application can be completed in as little as 15-20 minutes and the scholarship will award more than $50,000 in increments of $500-$1,000, issued to recipients in the form of a check to be used as desired. The scholarship is designed to identify and reward outstanding high school seniors who have demonstrated an ability to excel in the fields of academics, extra-curricular school activities and community involvement. It is available to any male, graduating senior who is enrolling in a four-year undergraduate college program.

name: Honors Graduation Design a Better Future Scholarship
description: Ever wondered just how much of a difference high school students can make on their communities? The winners from previous years have proven it can be profound. That's why the annual Design a Better Future scholarship continues to be a design-thinking, community-improvement project. Each year they fund up to five $10,000 tuition awards, with the top project receiving up to $5,000 to keep the project going. So design and work on a community improvement project and use their checklist as a guide.

name: O. Warren Hillgren Scholarship (La Cañada Flintridge Chamber of Commerce)
description: Sponsored by the La Cañada Flintridge Chamber of Commerce, this scholarship awards $1,500 to seniors in good standing at La Cañada High School who demonstrate bases of merit including, but not limited to, academics, character, extracurricular school activities, community service, and athletics. The application requires a written essay describing involvement and benefits received from their extracurricular school activities and community service including work in the local business community. Print and fill out the cover sheet and application, and turn in the completed application to Mrs. Proctor in the College & Career Center. Applicants who move forward will be interviewed after school in the C³ the following week.

name: Mary Ellen Hillgren (MEH) Scholarship (Action League of the Foothills)
description: Every year, Action League of the Foothills (formerly Assistance League of Flintridge) awards scholarships to La Cañada High School seniors who will be attending a four-year college or university in the fall. A committee of ALF members reviews the applications and selects the recipients, based on excellence in academics, character, extra-curricular activities and community service. The names of the recipients are engraved on a perpetual plaque that is displayed in the trophy case at the high school. Two Mary Ellen Hillgren Memorial Scholarships of $2,000 each shall be presented at the Senior Awards Ceremony at La Cañada High School. Return the application and the required essay to: Action League of the Foothills, Attn: Hillgren Scholarship, 4607 Oakwood Avenue, La Cañada Flintridge, CA 91011. Questions? Contact info@alflintridge.org or 818-790-1328.

name: Archer Rivas Foundation Scholarship
description: The Archer Rivas Foundation is a non-profit organization created by Ron Archer and Reggie Rivas, the owners of Archer Travel Service Inc. in La Crescenta. Established in 2022, this organization strives to assist people who are seeking to live a happy, productive and healthy lifestyle. ARF is now offering $10,000 college scholarships to one senior from 5 different area high schools including Crescenta Valley, La Cañada High School, Verdugo Hills, Glendale, and Hoover. Potential recipients must show financial need and strong academic performance. Students must submit an application, an essay detailing why they should be considered, and letters of reference. Many aspects of your high school career will be taken into consideration including GPA, attendance, participation in school clubs and or sports, extra curricular activities, and public service. Standout candidates will be selected to have an interview with the foundation's Board of Directors in order to choose the scholarship recipients.

name: Taiwanese American Scholarship Fund (TASF)
description: 10 $7,500 scholarships available (per year for 4 years) for high school seniors planning to attend a university/college in the fall. The TASF is focused on helping economically-challenged Taiwanese American students. For more information call (213) 624-6400 ext. 6 or email kfan@apcf.org.

name: Student-View Scholarship
description: The Student-View Scholarship program is offering one $10,000 scholarship, two $1,000 scholarships, and ten $500 scholarships. No minimum SAT/ACT score or GPA, no essay, no application fees! Simply log onto www.student-view.com and complete a 20 minute application survey about colleges in your area. The scholarships are awarded via a random drawing.

name: Eric & Christine Alegria Public Service Scholarship (GLAEF)
description: The Eric & Christine Alegria Public Service Scholarship is specifically designed for graduating Los Angeles County students passionate about pursuing studies and a career in public service, demonstrating both academic dedication and financial need. Selected Alegria Scholars will be awarded up to $2,500 to attend a 2- or 4-year college or university.

name: Spartan Booster Club Scholarship (LCHS Boosters)
description: As an extension of LCHS Spartan Boosters' mission to enhance extracurricular activities, academics and athletic programs for all students in grades 7 thru 12 at La Cañada High School, they are proud to award two (2) $1,500 scholarships to selected LCHS seniors whose paths to success have been enriched by the activities Boosters supports. See the site for eligibility criteria, requirements, and the application.

name: CalHOPE Courage Award Scholarship Program
description: Honorees will earn a $2,500 scholarship, and their comeback story - whether from injury, illness, family hardship, academic pressure, or other stressors - will be shared to inspire and encourage peers facing similar challenges. Who is eligible: California high school seniors scheduled to graduate who participate in varsity interscholastic athletics and have overcome personal adversity, including stress, anxiety, and mental health challenges. Deadline: rolling; students are encouraged to apply early to be considered for all monthly selections. The application period closes May 1.

name: LCHS PTSA Senior Scholarship
description: The LCHS 9-12 PTSA awards scholarship(s) to graduating seniors each year. The scholarships vary in amount from $250 to $1,000. Open to graduating LCHS seniors with current 9-12 PTSA membership planning to continue higher education and who are residents of California. (9-12 PTSA membership cards can be picked up from Mrs. Proctor in the College and Career Center.) The scholarship acknowledges students involved in community service and leadership. Applicants will need to provide a completed application, transcript, and references (one from a teacher, another from a non-relative adult such as a coach, mentor outside of school, etc.). Note: this is different from the First District PTA Commemorative Senior Scholarship and therefore another great local opportunity!

name: Cañada Auxiliary of Professionals (CAP) Scholarships (Action League of the Foothills)
description: CAP Scholarships will be granted to students who will be attending a two-year college or an accredited occupational program in the fall. To qualify for the scholarship, applicants must attend school in the La Cañada Flintridge area and graduate in June with a 2.5 GPA or better. The recipient will be selected on the basis of merit with consideration given to career goals, achievements, community service and/or school involvement, and character. Return application and materials to Cañada Auxiliary of Professionals of Action League of the Foothills, 4607 Oakwood Avenue, La Cañada Flintridge, CA 91011, along with a one-page personal essay, verification of grades, résumé, and one sealed letter of recommendation. Incomplete applications will not be considered.

name: The Hope Scholarship (Bank of Hope)
description: The Hope Scholarship awards $2,500 scholarships to graduating high school seniors who plan to enroll in a 2-year or 4-year college. The program is designed to support students who demonstrate strong academic performance and financial need.

name: Cameron Impact Scholarship (Bryan Cameron Education Foundation)
description: JUNIORS! The Cameron Impact Scholarship is a four-year, full-tuition, impact-driven undergraduate scholarship awarded annually to 10-15 exceptional high school students who have demonstrated excellence in leadership, community service, extracurricular activities, and academics. The Cameron Impact Scholar is unique among their peers in their desire to directly impact their communities and the world at large. The scholarship covers the full tuition, fees, and books at any accredited U.S. based college or university that the recipient chooses to attend. Applications open February 1 for current juniors and are reviewed on a rolling basis; a total of 3,000 completed and eligible applications are accepted, and the application closes when that limit is reached or on the May 1 deadline, whichever occurs first.

name: Language Connects Foundation Scholarship
description: Future teachers! This scholarship is meant for high school seniors who are committed to pursuing the language teaching profession in languages other than English.

name: Hana Uno Shepard Memorial Scholarship (Greater Los Angeles JACL)
description: GLA (Greater Los Angeles Chapter - Japanese American Citizens League) annually awards the Hana Uno Shepard Memorial Scholarship. Applicants must be a graduating high school senior with a high achievement record, from a single-parent family, of Japanese descent, and a resident of Los Angeles or Orange County. The scholarship may be applied to any college, university, community college, fine arts, or vocational school. GLA provides the scholarship recipient with 4 years of JACL student membership. A new application is posted each February. Questions? greaterlajacl@gmail.com. National JACL also provides a variety of other scholarships.

name: Ryder Buck Music Foundation Memorial Scholarship
description: The Ryder Buck Music Foundation's mission is to grant financial support to college-bound seniors at La Cañada High School interested in studying music, whether instrumental, vocal, or theatrical - "Celebrating Dedication to the Transformational Power of Music." Students need not plan to major in music, but they must have a plan to include it in their studies, and to share it with the world. Requirements include: submission of LCHS transcript, completed application, interview and three-minute audition. Students will have a 15-minute interview including a three-minute performance piece/audition after the deadline. The $1,000 scholarship will be awarded at the LCHS Senior Awards Night.

name: Christopher J. Kurdoghlian Memorial Scholarship
description: Criteria: graduating senior at La Cañada High School with at least three years in the choral program. Procedure for selection: send an unofficial copy of transcript and responses to three questions (What impact has music had in your life? Share an example illustrating how music plays a role. What are your post-graduation plans?) to kkurdoghlian@gmail.com, listing your name, phone number and email address alongside your responses. Scholarships will be awarded in the amount of $1,000 at Senior Awards Night. Learn more about Christopher at ckurdoghlian.com.

name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
description: An annual, global science video competition for high-school students. You've grasped an important scientific theory, concept or principle - now can you share your insight? An inventive video can get across complex material that would take pages of text to communicate. To take part in the Breakthrough Junior Challenge, create a short video (2:00 - two minutes max) to explain a big idea in one of these fields: Physics, Mathematics, or Life Sciences. Your film can take any form you like: animation, talking head, documentary, dramatic reconstruction, whatever. It's worth keeping in mind that video is a dynamic visual medium - using diagrams, simulations, physical demonstrations etc. is a lot more effective than standing in front of a blackboard talking. To show creativity, your film should be as original as possible. The competition begins in May and ends in September.

name: Kiwanis Club of La Cañada Flintridge Scholarship
description: Since 1948, the Kiwanis Club of La Cañada has been devoted to serving the children in our local community and also children all across the country and worldwide through unique and innovative service projects and fundraising initiatives. They are all passionate about making their community and the world a better place for children so they can thrive. Apply via the Kiwanis Club of LCF Scholarship Application link.

name: Against The Grain Groundbreaker Leadership Scholarship
description: Provides financial assistance and promotion of Asian American college seniors and graduate students who have exhibited exemplary leadership, vision, and passion that is blazing a trail for others to follow and changing lives in the Asian American community. Awards: $1,500 to be applied toward school tuition and fees.

name: Japanese American Treaty Centennial Scholarship Fund (JATCSF)
description: The Japanese American Treaty Centennial Scholarship Fund, Inc. (also known as the Japanese American Scholarship Fund) seeks applicants for the JATCSF scholarship award each year. This is open to graduating high school students of Japanese ancestry residing in Southern California who are planning to enroll in a 4-year college in the fall. Download the application form and instructions via JCCSC.com.

name: Altadena Photographers High School Scholarship for Eaton Fire Survivors
description: Altadena Photographers is sponsoring the High School Scholarship for Eaton Fire Survivors to support graduating seniors impacted by the Eaton Fire who may be pursuing careers in the arts at a college or trade school with an interest in visual art, including photography. They believe in the power of creativity to heal and rebuild, and this scholarship aims to provide financial assistance to the next generation of visual storytellers and makers. Please submit your application, teacher recommendation, and a three-piece portfolio to be considered for this award. The award is $250.

name: Abbott and Fenner Scholarship
description: Open to Juniors and Seniors! Abbott & Fenner offer this $1,000 scholarship because they are committed to helping those who have the desire and ambition to succeed. Applicants must write an essay on the topic: Describe your educational career and life goals. Explain your plan for achieving these goals. Include your degree/major, why you selected it, and how this degree/major will help you achieve your goals. The essay should be between 500 and 1,000 words. Submissions must be sent by email to scholarships at abbottandfenner.com.

name: Big Sun Athletics Scholarship
description: Big Sun Athletics' goal is to help young athletes succeed in their academic pursuits by offering an annual $500 scholarship to a deserving student. All student athletes are eligible regardless of the sport they are engaged in or the capacity in which they participate. The student must be a high school senior or be attending a post secondary institute. Send a short essay (500-1,000 words) answering: How did your participation in sports during your high school years influence you? Has your participation influenced your career goals? Has your participation influenced how you relate to your family? Send your essay, with your name, and let them know you play a sport at La Cañada High School, to athleticawards@bigsunathletics.com.

name: Marcus Stroman Scholarship (bold.org)
description: 2 $25,000 winners. To apply, students must submit an essay and video describing the college of their dreams, why they wish to continue their education at that university, and how the 2025 wildfires have impacted their goals and aspirations. High school seniors from Pasadena or Altadena with a 3.0+ GPA are eligible to apply for this scholarship. Selection criteria: Ambition, Drive, Impact. Understanding the immense challenges students face, New York Yankees pitcher Marcus Stroman established the Marcus Stroman Scholarship, an initiative of his Height Doesn't Measure Heart (HDMH) Foundation. The HDMH Foundation is dedicated to empowering in-need youth, helping them rise above their circumstances, reach their full potential, and achieve their dreams.

name: Women in Public Finance Los Angeles Chapter Scholarship
description: Two recipients are awarded a $2,500 scholarship. To qualify and apply for the Scholarship and Award, the applicant must, at a minimum: 1. Be a female high school senior who intends to attend college in the fall. 2. Have at least a 3.0 GPA, or equivalent. 3. Exhibit leadership skills through extracurricular activities, volunteer positions, and/or work experience. 4. Have an interest in pursuing a public finance related career in finance, government, nonprofits, or law. 5. Complete and email the scholarship application form, the required essays and a photocopy of your most recent unofficial high school transcript to wpflascholarship@gmail.com. 6. Los Angeles County residency required - either lives or attends high school within Los Angeles County.

name: "Be Bold" No-Essay Scholarship (bold.org)
description: The $25,000 "Be Bold" Scholarship is a no-essay scholarship that will be awarded to the applicant with the boldest profile. To Bold.org, boldest does not mean "best", or "most accomplished". Being bold means being: Earnest, Determined, and Moving. Furthermore, this scholarship will be similar to the many easy scholarships available on Bold.org in that it will favor students who apply earlier - who are bold and seize the day without procrastinating. Only one person will be selected.

name: Jewish Federation of the Greater San Gabriel and Pomona Valleys Scholarship
description: The Jewish Federation of the Greater San Gabriel and Pomona Valleys ("the Jewish Federation SGPV") will award a scholarship in the amount of $2,500 to a current junior (or most recently having completed their junior year) high school student. The scholarship will be sent to the college the student will attend following completion of high school. Criteria: academic achievement, Jewish community involvement, general community service, leadership, extra-curricular activities, work experience. Eligibility: the applicant must be a high school student who is planning to attend a 4-year college or university after high school graduation. A minimum unweighted cumulative GPA of 3.0 is required. Application packets should be sent to: Jewish Federation of the Greater San Gabriel and Pomona Valleys, 114A W. Lime Avenue, Monrovia, CA 91016. Questions: federation@jewishsgpv.org or 626.445.0810.

name: Sutliff & Stout "First Step" to Distraction-Free Driving Scholarship
description: In an effort to reduce the devastating consequences of distracted driving among young drivers, the lawyers at Sutliff & Stout are offering a $1,500 scholarship to students. They are asking students to write an essay of at least 500 words detailing their most common distracted driving habits, and to describe the concrete steps they will take to put an end to those habits. See the site for eligibility, requirements, and the application link.

name: Niche $10,000 No Essay Scholarship
description: Niche is awarding one student $10,000 to help cover tuition, housing, books and other college expenses - no essay required! High school seniors who apply can also be eligible to receive acceptance (and scholarship!) offers from Niche Direct Admissions® partner colleges. Apply for the $10,000 No Essay Scholarship and focus on your education, not your finances. The winner is selected by random drawing.

name: 10x Digital Marketing Scholarship
description: If you're a senior going into a business, tech, marketing or communications degree, 10x Digital is awarding $4,000 to students planning to go into a field related to digital marketing. In order to qualify, you must be a high school senior that plans to take 10 credit hours during the spring semester in a field relating to digital marketing. To apply, write an essay of 500 words regarding your life story, your field of study, career, and how you plan to make an impact on the world.

name: ScholarshipOwl No Essay Scholarship
description: Applicants must be 16 years of age or older and enrolled, within 3 months of registration in the Scholarship Sweepstakes, at a qualified high school, college or university within the United States. In order to apply you must create an account on ScholarshipOwl. As said in the name, no essay is required.

name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program Scholarship
description: The Coca-Cola Scholars Foundation Scholarship is an achievement-based scholarship awarded to students in their final year of high school. Students are recognized for their capacity to lead and serve, as well as their commitment to making a significant impact on their schools and communities. 150 Coca-Cola Scholars are selected each year to receive this $20,000 scholarship. The application opens August 1 each year.

name: QuestBridge National College Match Scholarship
description: Recipients can be admitted early to one of QuestBridge's college partners with a full ride scholarship of $325,000. It covers all years at their college partner with early admission. Applicants must be high school seniors planning to enroll in college in the fall and come from low income households earning less than $65,000/year for a family of four. The application opens in late July.

name: Chicago Culinary Museum Scholarship
description: The Chicago Culinary Museum uses their scholarship to promote and celebrate Chicago as a Culinary Mecca. To support their mission, the Chicago Culinary Museum and Chef's Hall of Fame offers two scholarships annually for tuition to students currently enrolled in an accredited Culinary or Hospitality Management program. The scholarship award will have an annual value of up to $500 for an accredited Culinary or Hospitality Management program.

name: American Quarter Horse Foundation Scholarships
description: The American Quarter Horse Foundation connects horses and people through charitable giving to support programs that preserve our horse's legacy and further the well-being of the American Quarter Horse and the Quarter Horse family. Different grants are offered for different programs. If you have a passion for equestrianism, apply. Deadlines vary by program (earliest October 1 and latest January 15, 11:59 pm GMT).

name: Applied/GRAITEC Sustainability Scholarship Essay Contest (ASTI)
description: The Applied/GRAITEC Sustainability Scholarship Program is an achievement-based scholarship awarded to students in their last two years of high school. Students are recognized for their ability to grasp sustainability in the construction industry, develop research skills to comprehend and address significant problems, demonstrate creative thinking for solutions, and consider the challenges in implementing the solutions. Empowering Young Innovators: the program empowers young innovators attending a high school in the US. Students with the most compelling essays on innovative and sustainable solutions can win scholarships ranging from $250 to $1,500 based on their performance.

name: Fred J. Miller Memorial Music Education Fund Scholarship (Music for All)
description: The Fred J. Miller Memorial Music Education Fund was set up to support future music educators in honor of Fred's life's work, talent, and passion for the marching arts. Mr. Miller's legacy will continue to live on through the many students who will benefit from this scholarship. This annual scholarship will be awarded to a student nominated by their director of bands. The student must have also performed at one of the Bands of America Regional, Super Regional, or Grand National Championships. The award of $2,000 is made possible through the generosity of the Fred J. Miller Memorial Music Education Fund and the Miller family. The scholarship is announced and presented during the Grand National Finals Awards Ceremony.

name: Pacific Century Institute Los Angeles Project Bridge Youth Ambassador Program
description: For JUNIORS & SENIORS! Established in 1993 after the Los Angeles Riots (SAIGU) took place, Los Angeles based Pacific Century Institute in conjunction with New York based Korea Society will select 16 students (eight from Los Angeles and eight from New York). The goal of Project Bridge is to instill a sense of understanding and respect to "bridge" the gap between cultures through simultaneous teachings of cultural awareness and leadership skills. Throughout the year-long academic year, Los Angeles and New York students attend different bi-weekly workshops focusing on topics such as: building and strengthening leadership skills through presentation and public speaking; education on intercultural understanding on race, ethnicity, nationality, and culture; education on Korea and its culture, history, language, economy, and policy; and the 1992 LA Riots, which deeply affected the area's Korean American community. The highlight of Project Bridge is a fully subsidized ten-day study tour in South Korea.

name: Music for All Foundation Scholarship (Yamaha and Fred J. Miller Family)
description: These one-time awards honor students nominated by the directors of bands performing at Grand National Championships. The awards are made possible through generous gifts from Yamaha Corporation of America ($1,000 Yamaha Scholarship) and the Fred J. Miller Family ($1,000 Fred J. Miller Family Scholarship). The scholarships are announced and presented at the Grand National Finals Awards Ceremony. Each school's band director may nominate two students from their band. Directors should complete the nomination form and return it with the required attachments to Music for All.

name: Miss La Cañada Flintridge Royal Court Scholarship
description: Applications are open for the Miss La Cañada Flintridge Royal Court. Juniors only. Miss La Cañada Flintridge will receive a $1,000 scholarship and each court member will receive a $500 scholarship from the La Cañada Flintridge Chamber of Commerce and Community Association, along with several gifts from local merchants. The deadline to apply is 4 pm on October 30th at the Chamber Office.

name: VFW Voice of Democracy Scholarship
description: Established in 1947, the VFW's Voice of Democracy audio-essay program provides high school students with the unique opportunity to express themselves in regards to a democratic and patriotic-themed recorded essay. The national first place winner receives a $35,000 scholarship paid directly to the recipient's American university, college or vocational/technical school. A complete list of other national scholarships range from $1,000-$21,000, and the first place winner from each VFW Department (state) wins at least a scholarship of $1,000. Before submitting your essay, read the rules and eligibility requirements, and find your sponsoring local VFW Post, as applications must be turned in to a Post by midnight, October 31.

name: Hispanic Heritage Foundation Youth Awards
description: This scholarship was founded by the Hispanic Heritage Foundation, honoring Latino high school seniors who excel academically and in other extracurriculars. Gold, Silver, and Bronze recipients are selected to receive a one-time grant to fund their college education or to fund a community service effort that tackles a social issue. Recipients will be celebrated in 10 virtual ceremonies and will be part of the HHF network. To be eligible, you must be a senior with a minimum of a 3.0 GPA and be of Hispanic heritage (including Spain, Brazil, Philippines).

name: Stephen J. Brady Stop Hunger Scholarship
description: Students ages 5 to 25 who are using their skills and volunteering to fight hunger in their communities within the last 12 months have the opportunity to receive a $10,000 scholarship and a $5,000 grant for their hunger-related charity. Winners will also get an all-expenses-paid trip to go to the foundation's fundraising event (Sodexo Charity Classic) in Frisco, Texas.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
description: Regeneron STS is the nation's oldest and most prestigious science research competition for high school students. Started in 1942 as the Westinghouse Science Talent Search, Regeneron STS recognizes and empowers our nation's most promising young scientists who are developing ideas that could solve society's most urgent challenges. Each year, around 2,000 students enter the Regeneron STS, submitting original research in critically important scientific fields of study and a full application for holistic review. Unique among high school competitions, the Regeneron STS focuses on identifying, inspiring, and engaging the nation's most promising future leaders in STEM.

name: Track to the Trades Scholarship (bold.org)
description: This scholarship is aimed to support current and future tradespeople for people going to vocational schools. To be eligible for this scholarship of $2,500, applicants must be a high school senior planning to go into trade school embodying the qualities of generosity, respect, innovation, and teamwork. Applicants must write an essay to apply.

name: Kimberly Dawn Ellis Scholarship (Jewish Federation of the Greater San Gabriel and Pomona Valleys)
description: Kimberly attended the University of California at Santa Barbara and majored in Law and Society. After graduating from UCSB with honors in 1997, she attended Pepperdine Law School. In addition to her academic achievement, her strong Jewish commitment was shown through her involvement in B'nai Brith Youth Organization (BBYO) and Jewish day camp. While attending Pepperdine Law School, she was killed on December 9, 1997, by a drunk driver. A $500 scholarship is being offered by her family for future college students to perpetuate her memory. Application packets should be sent to: Jewish Federation of the Greater San Gabriel and Pomona Valleys, 114A W. Lime Avenue, Monrovia, CA 91016.

name: Dr. Robert Hawkins Memorial Scholarship (John Philip Sousa Foundation)
description: Dr. Hawkins was a highly achieved band director in the United States. He was named one of the ten outstanding band directors in the US in 1972. In his honor, this $1,000 national scholarship was made for students working towards a degree in instrumental (band) music education planning to attend a college in the United States. The application form is linked for further information.

name: Kanoski Bresney Stand Up to Distracted Driving Scholarship
description: Thousands of drivers, especially young adults and teenagers, fall victim to distracted driving and result in deaths that could have been prevented. To support students who do their part to fight the problem of distracted driving, Kanoski Bresney presents a $4,000 scholarship for high school seniors who have a current overall GPA of at least 3.0 to submit a 1,000 word essay about distracted driving in young drivers.

name: GreenPal Business Scholarship (Scholarship for Tomorrow's Entrepreneur)
description: The GreenPal Business Scholarship is designed to help motivated, driven students to accomplish their vision as a future business leader. $2,000 will be paid equally over 4 semesters for students who have put together a business plan or who own/operate their own business, are in the graduating senior class with a 3.5+ GPA, and are driven to be a business owner or entrepreneur with a declared major or minor in Business, Economics, or Finance. Applicants will email their essay (500-1,000 words) along with a photo to GreenPal.

name: The NHS Scholarship (National Honor Society)
description: The National Association of Secondary School Principals (NASSP) is awarding $2 million in scholarships to 600 students. Each year, scholarship recipients are selected based on their demonstration of the four pillars of NHS: Scholarship, Service, Leadership, and Character. The top 25 scholarship finalists and their advisers receive an all-expense paid trip to Washington, D.C. for Trailblazing Leadership Week.

name: National Press Club Journalism Institute Scholarships
description: There are several different opportunities available with various deadline dates. Student journalists, like their professional colleagues, dedicate themselves to covering their communities across platforms. Juggling classwork, part-time work, and journalism activities can often go without reward. The National Press Club and NPC Journalism Institute are proud to administer four scholarships honoring promising future journalists serving their communities.

name: Kaiser Permanente Health Equity Scholars Program
description: The Kaiser Permanente Health Equity Scholars Program is designed to assist students who are planning to pursue a career in the healthcare industry. Students must have a demonstrated interest in pursuing a clinical (e.g., pharmacist, physician, practitioner, nurse) or non-clinical (e.g., accounting, business administration, human resources, marketing, public policy) career in healthcare. Selected students will receive a $2,500 award.

name: Hagan Scholarship
description: A need-based merit scholarship for achieving, goal-driven students. Recipients receive $2,000 to purchase essentials for college, up to $7,500 each semester for up to 8 consecutive semesters, a study abroad opportunity worth up to $8,000, a Schwab brokerage account to learn how to invest, and free workshops to learn important life skills not typically covered in college. Eligibility: must attend high school in the US, must have a 3.50 cumulative GPA, and more (see the Hagan Scholarship Foundation site for full requirements).

name: Ron Brown Scholar Program
description: The Ron Brown Scholar Program awards 45 college scholarships annually in the amount of $40,000 to extraordinary African American high school seniors. Students must attend a four-year accredited college or university within the United States. Since 1996, the Program has awarded more than 500 scholarships.

name: Ray Stoesser Memorial Scholarship (US Rice Producers Association)
description: This $5,000 scholarship is being offered by the Stoesser family in partnership with the US Rice Producers Association to college students being interested in or currently pursuing a career in an agriculture-related field. In addition to this scholarship, the selected recipient will be a student ambassador for USRPA, expected to participate in 2 activities during the year. Applicants will submit an online form and a video no longer than 5 minutes on the prompts provided.

name: Rubincam Youth Writing Competition (National Genealogical Society)
description: The Rubincam Youth Writing Competition was made to honor Milton Rubincam for his work in the field of genealogy. These awards are to recognize the youth as the next generation of family historians. The selected winner gets a $500 prize, a plaque, and an NGS membership. The person is expected to be a high school student who has an interest in becoming a family historian.

name: The Coolidge Scholarship
description: For Juniors! A full-ride, four-year, merit scholarship that may be used by recipients for undergraduate study at any accredited college or university in the U.S. Any current high school JUNIOR who plans to enroll in college in the fall of the following year may apply. Academic excellence is the primary criterion considered by the Coolidge Scholarship. Secondary criteria include an interest in public policy and an appreciation of the values President Coolidge championed. Successful candidates will also demonstrate humility and have a record of genuine service to their communities. Alert: candidates are required to read President Coolidge's Autobiography and complete a few other reading assignments, so start early.

name: Glenn Michelson Memorial Award Essay Contest (CSF)
description: The Glenn Michelson Memorial Award was established in 2012 in memory of the late Glenn Michelson, past 20-year CSF adviser of Sequoia High School in Redwood City and past Board of Directors member who served as State President, CSF Registrar, Regional Vice-President, Historian, and Legislative Chair. He was a strong advocate of the CSF motto promoting community service. Upon his passing, Glenn bequeathed funds to CSF, and the Board of Directors voted to have an annual essay contest in Glenn's honor open to high school CSF juniors and seniors who have a passion for service. All Junior and Senior CSF members may apply. Submissions are accepted beginning November 1st each year; chapter dues must be paid and course lists submitted prior to submitting essays.

name: AIAA Lockheed Martin Marilyn Hewson Scholarship
description: This scholarship was created to encourage young women to study aerospace engineering and pursue a career in the aerospace defense industry. Open to a United States high school senior intending to pursue an aerospace STEM major in aerospace engineering, computer engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, industrial engineering, mathematics, mechanical engineering, or physics.
